symptom: `exec --continue-on-error` of a MOVE ENTITY whose target write was refused reported the statement failed, and the entity was in neither module: removed from the source, not in the target. 12 chained moves on a generated project lost 9 entities and mx check then reported 53 'no longer exists' errors.
cause: MoveEntity persisted the source domain model, then built and persisted the target; a refusal of the target came after the source was on disk. The default exec rolls the whole script back, so only --continue-on-error kept the half-done move.
insight: **A statement that writes two units must decide both before writing either.** Both domain models are now built and encoded first and checked against the refusals the write path makes on content alone (canon.DuplicateElementIDError, canon.BareAttributeRefError); a target write that fails anyway restores the source's stored bytes with UpdateRawUnitPatch (no transplant onto the restore). The test provokes the refusal the way #2322 did — an element in the target with the moved entity's $ID — and without the fix it reports exactly the symptom ('entity Account is gone from Administration'). With #2322 fixed the reported chain no longer reaches the refusal, which is why the test plants one.
